question: Why did the error rate go up on 03 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The auth feature flag change increased error rate.
why_chain: The auth feature flag was changed to 50% in eu-west.
This change affected the error rate for service auth.
The error rate increased from 0.39% to 5.06%.

contributing_factors.description: Upstream identity-db service failure caused the error rate increase.
why_chain: The upstream identity-db service returned HTTP 503 for auth.
This caused the auth service to timeout and fail.
The auth service then had a higher error rate.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in request volume caused the error rate increase.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume for service auth stayed about the same.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency caused the error rate increase.
ruled_out.reason: The p95 latency for service auth rose, but the error rate increased more.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The log error messages were the root cause.
ruled_out.reason: The log error messages occurred after the change and are symptoms, not causes.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service auth rose from 0.39% to 5.06% (+1196%), with a change point at 2026-03-03T06:55:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service auth: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.06).
At the same time, request volume for service auth stayed about the same (1082 per 5 min before, 1303 per 5 min after, +20%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service auth rose (91 ms before, 162 ms after, +79%).
Changed auth feature flag new_ui_flow to 50% in eu-west (auth, eu-west; 2 min before the change; record R012; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
Upstream identity-db returning HTTP 503 for auth (auth; 5 min after the change; record R014; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
auth: ERROR upstream identity-db timeout after 3 retries (auth, ap-south; 1 min after the change; record R013; fit: describes a symptom, not a change)
auth: ERROR upstream identity-db timeout after 3 retries (auth, us-east; 7 min after the change; record R015; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
auth: ERROR upstream identity-db timeout after 3 retries (auth, eu-west; 15 min after the change; record R016; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

reasons: ✓ A change event (config_changes) lines up in time (2 min before the change).
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✗ 1 other change event(s) fit about as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
✗ Two or more changes fit equally well, so the cause cannot be confirmed.
missing_data: Details to tell the competing changes apart (e.g. a rollback test)

actions.action: Roll back the auth feature flag change to 50% and monitor the error rate.
Monitor the upstream identity-db service and ensure it is stable.
Review and optimize the error handling in the auth service.
